formats.key: Session(address owner,address delegate,uint48 validAfter,uint48 validUntil,uint32 maxCalls,uint16 maxFeeBps,AssetLimit[] limits,bytes32 salt)AssetLimit(address token,uint256 limit)
effects: Anyone who holds the signature can call createSessionBySig to create a session in the owner's name. The signature has no deadline and no nonce.
The delegate gets the right to sign per-call intents. Allowlisted target contracts (e.g. MintAndRedeem) then execute those intents for the owner.
For each listed token, the session gets a spend allowance equal to `limit`. A limit of type(uint256).max is never decremented, so it is unlimited.
The session is valid from validAfter to validUntil. A validUntil of 0 means the session never expires.
The delegate can sign at most maxCalls calls. A maxCalls of 0 means unlimited calls (only allowed when validUntil is not 0).
Relayers can take a fee of up to maxFeeBps of the output amount, from what the owner receives.
Once the session is created, only the owner can revoke it, with revokeSession or revokeSessionBySig.
formats.shown: "Create ftUSD session" / "ftUSD session <delegate>", with the owner, delegate, valid-after and valid-until dates, max calls (raw), max fee in bps, and one token limit per listed token.

findings.title: Session intent does not say the delegate can spend the owner's tokens through target contracts.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "intent": "Create ftUSD session", "interpolatedIntent": "ftUSD session {delegate}". SessionManager.sol devdoc: "Delegate signs per-call intents (EIP-712) that are consumed by trusted target contracts (e.g. MintAndRedeem)"; validateAndConsume decrements tokenAllowance[sessionId][spendToken].
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Let delegate spend tokens for you" and the interpolatedIntent to "Allow {delegate} to act and spend tokens for you until {validUntil}".

findings.title: Session validUntil of 0 means no expiry but renders as the 1970 epoch date.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol SessionConfig: "uint48 validUntil; // 0 = no expiry"; validateAndConsume: "if (s.validUntil != 0 && nowTs > s.validUntil)". descriptor field validUntil: format "date", encoding "timestamp", no special-value handling.
findings.fix: Show 0 as "No expiry", e.g. with a threshold/message or an enum-style label, or add a separate notice when validUntil is 0.

findings.title: Session maxCalls of 0 means unlimited calls but is shown as the raw number 0.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol: "uint32 maxCalls; // 0 = unlimited (requires validUntil != 0)"; validateAndConsume: "if (s.maxCalls != 0 && expectedNonce >= s.maxCalls)". descriptor: maxCalls "format": "raw".
findings.fix: Label 0 as "Unlimited" for maxCalls (e.g. an enum or map with 0 -> "Unlimited").

findings.title: Session token limit renders as a raw 1e20 number and never names the token.
findings.evidence: case 0 screen: {"label": "Token limit", "value": "100000000000000000000"} for token 0xF7D85EC4E7710f71992752eac2111312e73E9C9C. The descriptor has no field for limits.[].token. It is only used as the tokenPath.
findings.fix: Add a field {"path": "limits.[].token", "label": "Token", "format": "addressName", "params": {"types": ["token"]}} before the limit, so the token is named even when its metadata does not resolve.

findings.title: Session "Max fee" does not say it is a relayer fee taken from the signer's output.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol: "uint16 maxFeeBps; // max relayer fee vs output amount (0 = no fee)". descriptor: label "Max fee", unit base "bps", decimals 0; case 0 renders "500bps".
findings.fix: Use label "Max relayer fee (of output)" and params {"base": "%", "decimals": 2} so 500 renders as 5%.

findings.title: Session signature does not limit which target contracts or actions the delegate can run.
findings.evidence: validateAndConsume: "if (!allowedTarget[msg.sender]) revert TargetNotAllowed(msg.sender);". allowedTarget is set by the contract owner through setAllowedTarget. Calls with spendAmount 0 skip the per-asset limit check.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show the allowlist. Name the known target actions (mint/redeem ftUSD) in the intent or in the descriptor metadata.

findings.title: Session signature has no deadline or nonce, so anyone can submit it at any later time.
findings.evidence: createSessionBySig: the digest covers owner_, delegate, validAfter, validUntil, maxCalls, maxFeeBps, limitsHash and salt only. revokeSession requires "s.owner == address(0) revert SessionNotFound", so the signer cannot cancel the signature before someone submits it.

findings.title: Session test does not cover validUntil 0, maxCalls 0 or an unlimited token limit.
findings.evidence: case 0 uses validUntil 1770600000, maxCalls 100 and limit 1e20 only. The "Unlimited" threshold message and the 0 special values in _createSession / validateAndConsume are not tested.
findings.fix: Add cases with validUntil 0 and maxCalls>0, with maxCalls 0, and with limit type(uint256).max, plus a known token so the amount renders with a ticker.

couldNotCheck: The allowlisted target contracts that consume sessions and move the owner's tokens (e.g. MintAndRedeem) are not in the directory. I could not check that they report every spend to validateAndConsume or that they enforce maxFeeBps.
